so.subjective:
* Patient reports a painful and unstable knee injury sustained while skiing last weekend, which occurred when she caught her ski and fell, causing her knee to pop.
* The patient, Michelle, is 34 years old.
* She has not experienced any previous knee injuries or surgeries.
* The patient reports that the knee pain feels like it won't hold their weight and has been present since the fall.
* The patient reports that their toes feel okay and they can still move them normally.
* The patient reports having undergone an X-ray, which did not reveal any bone issues, but has not yet had an MRI.
* She did not notice any immediate swelling or bruising after the injury, but her knee has been swollen and painful since.
* She reports pain on the outside of her knee, near the lateral side, which worsens with attempts to straighten her leg.
* She has not experienced any numbness, tingling, or changes in the color or temperature of her leg or foot.
* She has not noticed any locking or clicking sensations in her knee since the injury.

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: Hi, I'm Michelle, and I'm 34. I injured my knee while skiing last weekend, and it's been really painful and unstable since then. I can't bear weight on it, and I had to be taken down by the ski patrol.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Can you describe the exact mechanism of the knee injury, such as whether you twisted your knee, landed awkwardly, or hit it on something? Also, have you experienced any previous knee injuries or surgeries?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: I was skiing in Vermont, and I caught my ski when I was coming off the lift, which made me fall. My knee popped, and it's hurt ever since. I don't think I've ever had a previous knee injury or surgery.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Did you experience any immediate swelling or bruising after the injury, and if so, when did it occur?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: I didn't notice any immediate swelling or bruising right after the fall, but it's been pretty swollen and painful ever since. I haven't really looked at it closely for bruising, to be honest.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you experienced any locking, clicking, or giving way of the knee since the injury?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: Yes, the knee feels like it's going to buckle when I try to put weight on it, and it's been really unstable. I haven't noticed any locking or clicking, just a constant pain on the outside and the feeling that it won't hold me up.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you undergone any imaging studies, such as an X-ray or MRI, for this knee injury?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: I haven't had an MRI yet, but I did have an X-ray done, and it didn't show any bone issues. The doctor wants to order an MRI to check for ligament damage, like maybe an ACL tear.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Could you please describe the exact location of the pain on your knee and whether it radiates to any other part of your leg?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: The pain is on the outside of my knee, near the lateral side, and it doesn't really radiate anywhere else. It's pretty focused right there, and it hurts a lot when I try to straighten my leg all the way.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Could you describe any numbness, tingling, or weakness in your leg or foot? Have you noticed any changes in the color or temperature of your leg?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: I don't have any numbness or tingling in my leg or foot, and I don't notice any changes in the color or temperature of my leg. My toes feel okay, and I can still move them normally.
